questions: Should we delete edges to achieve any forest, or specifically a forest that is a spanning forest (i.e., includes all vertices)?
If multiple forests are possible, does the answer require the minimum number of deletions across all possible resulting forests?
Is the resulting forest allowed to be disconnected (i.e., a collection of trees)?
Are we allowed to delete zero edges if the graph is already a forest?
Should we consider edge deletions that might leave the graph with isolated vertices, or is the goal to keep as many edges as possible while removing cycles?
Does 'simple undirected graph' imply no self-loops or multiple edges, and does that restriction apply to the resulting forest as well?
If the graph has multiple connected components, do we treat each component independently for cycle removal?
Is the answer simply M - (N - number_of_connected_components), i.e., remove edges until each component is a tree?
